_comment: Byte-exact encode/decode pairs for the ESP->Pico SAFETY_CMD_PUSH_CONTEXT (0x07) payload, per docs/LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 4. payload_hex is the raw command payload as it would sit inside kilnlink_frame_t.payload -- it does NOT include the outer frame header/CRC/stuffing, which is kilnlink_frame's job (see frame_vectors.json). Generated by hand-computing struct.pack('<f'/'<I') in Python and cross-checked against kilnlink_context_encode/decode in test/test_context.c.

vectors.name: two_zones
vectors.note: flags = PROFILE_RUNNING|HEAT_REQUESTED|CONTEXT_VALID (0x0D). Zone 1's measured_c is NaN (a guard-tripped, invalid-reading zone) -- exercises that a NaN float round-trips bit-for-bit rather than being 'fixed up' to 0.

vectors.name: zero_zones
vectors.note: zone_count = 0 -- the fixed 15-byte header with no zone blocks at all. flags = 0 (no profile running, nothing faulted, no heat requested, context not even marked valid -- the 'ESP just booted, has nothing to report yet' case).

hostile_vectors.name: wrong_cmd
hostile_vectors.note: Byte 0 is 0x09 (SET_FIRING_CEILING's id), not 0x07 -- a well-formed 15-byte PUSH_CONTEXT-shaped buffer whose command byte says it's actually a different frame type.

hostile_vectors.name: zone_count_out_of_range
hostile_vectors.note: zone_count byte (offset 14) is 4, past KILNLINK_CONTEXT_MAX_ZONES (3) -- must be rejected before any zone block is read, regardless of how many bytes actually follow.

hostile_vectors.name: length_mismatch_one_zone_claimed_zero_bytes_present
hostile_vectors.note: zone_count says 1 (needs 15+14=29 bytes) but the buffer is only the 15-byte fixed header -- a length byte that promises more than actually arrived.
